idiom_name: queue.Queue(maxsize=N) with blocking put/get and task_done/join
implementation_notes: The standard library's queue module implements multi-producer, multi-consumer queues with all locking built in: Queue(maxsize=N).put(item) blocks while full and .get() blocks while empty, put_nowait/get_nowait raise queue.Full/queue.Empty for the non-blocking form, and task_done()/join() track outstanding work (join() unblocks when every put has a matching task_done and raises ValueError on over-counting). Shutdown is explicit since Python 3.13 (shutdown() makes further put/get calls raise ShutDown and optionally drains the queue); before that, one sentinel per consumer ends the loops. SimpleQueue is the reentrant unbounded FIFO for callbacks/destructors, and multiprocessing.Queue is the cross-process form. The GIL limits CPU-bound parallelism, so the queue buys rate decoupling and I/O overlap.
code_sketch:
import queue, threading

jobs = queue.Queue(maxsize=1000)

def consume():
    while (job := jobs.get()) is not None:   # None = sentinel
        handle(job)
        jobs.task_done()

threading.Thread(target=consume, daemon=True).start()
jobs.put(job)                                # blocks while full
pitfalls: maxsize=0 (the default) is unbounded; the bound must be set explicitly or memory grows with the producer's speed.
One sentinel per consumer, or Queue.shutdown() (3.13+): a single sentinel with several consumers leaves the others blocked forever.
task_done() called more often than get() raises ValueError, and exception paths that skip it leave join() hanging.
Python threads do not run CPU-bound code in parallel (GIL): the queue gives rate decoupling and I/O overlap, not parallel compute.

variants.name: asyncio.Queue between tasks
variants.idiom_name: asyncio.Queue(maxsize=N) with await put/get and task_done/join
variants.implementation_notes: asyncio queues are the async/await analogue of the queue module and are not thread-safe: await queue.put(item) suspends the coroutine while the queue is full, await queue.get() suspends while it is empty, and worker tasks (asyncio.create_task) drain it on one event loop; join()/task_done() work as in the threaded form, there is no timeout parameter (wrap the await in asyncio.wait_for), and shutdown() (3.13+) raises QueueShutDown for blocked put/get callers. Use it when producers and consumers are coroutines: one thread, cooperative backpressure, and no lock machinery; move genuinely blocking work off the loop with asyncio.to_thread.
variants.code_sketch:
import asyncio

queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=1000)

async def worker():
    while True:
        item = await queue.get()
        if item is None: return         # sentinel
        await handle(item)
        queue.task_done()

asyncio.create_task(worker())
await queue.put(item)                   # suspends while full
pitfalls: asyncio.Queue is not thread-safe; calling put/get from another thread corrupts the loop - use loop.call_soon_threadsafe or asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe.
A blocking call (time.sleep, a blocking client) inside a consumer stalls every other task on the loop; use awaitable I/O or asyncio.to_thread.
maxsize=0 (the default) is unbounded and removes backpressure.
